period: Scholars generally place him in the 7th century CE, around the time of Kumarila; their exact chronological relation is debated.
context: Prabhakara, called Guru in the tradition, founded the Prabhakara school of Purva Mimamsa through his commentaries on Shabara's Bhashya. Tradition makes him a pupil of Kumarila, but scholars treat this as uncertain. His school was developed especially by Shalikanatha and remained a rival to the Bhatta school, though it had fewer followers in later centuries.
coreIdeas: Five means of valid knowledge; non-apprehension is not accepted as a separate pramana
Words convey meaning only as already related within a sentence, especially to an injunction (anvitabhidhana)
All cognition is valid; error is a failure to distinguish two cognitions, not a positive misapprehension (akhyati)
Every cognition reveals itself, its object and the knowing self together
Vedic injunction is binding as duty itself, not merely for the sake of its results

disagreements.note: The two Mimamsa schools differ on the pramanas, on the theory of sentence meaning, on the explanation of error, and on how the self is known.
